newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian unions report progress at budget talks.
newsitem.headline: Italian unions report progress at budget talks.

text.p: Talks between Italian unions and Prime Minister Romano Prodi over the 1997 budget made progress but a further meeting will be needed to clarify remaining problems, a leader of one of Italy's big three unions said.

"A final response to a possible general mobilisation (of members) will depend on a new meeting to be held before November 12 which will discuss government fiscal plans," Pietro Larizza, leader of the Uil union, told a news conference.
The leaders of Italy's three main unions, the Cigl, Cisl and Uil, met Prodi last week and afterwards threatened to launch strike action over the 1997 austerity budget.
A fresh meeting was held on Monday. "This time we made progress but the process of clarification is not complete," Larizza told reporters.
The unions are particularly anxious about possible cuts to welfare spending and plans to increase the tax burden next year.

They have also demanded reassurances that the centre-left government will not bring forward a review of a 1995 pension reform to 1997 and want Prodi to enact a labour pact signed last month which is designed to boost employment.

The 62.5 trillion lire deficit cutting budget is currently passing through the lower house of parliament, where a final vote is expected by November 17. It will then pass to the upper house for further ratification. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
